recommendations.title: `_prompt_reuse_saved_review()` in `plan_tool/cli/review_cmd.py` (step 7 "Keep unsafe sidecars out of reconcile-plan reus
recommendations.body: `_prompt_reuse_saved_review()` in `plan_tool/cli/review_cmd.py` (step 7 "Keep unsafe sidecars out of reconcile-plan reuse") prints `"{prefix} walking saved review"` on the `not sys.stdin.isatty()` arm, but `_cmd_review_body()` then reports the findings and returns without entering `walk_recommendations`, so a CI log reads `(reuse) walking saved review` immediately followed by `non-interactive stdin: skipping the walk`. The step's acceptance criterion pins the non-TTY path as report-and-return, so the announcement claims an action that never runs
recommendations.suggested_action: in `_prompt_reuse_saved_review()`, select the verb from `sys.stdin.isatty()` — print `reusing saved review` on the non-TTY arm and keep `walking saved review` for the `--reuse` / `--yes` TTY arms

recommendations.title: `RUNBOOK.md` § "Reuse-last-review prompt" ends with "The prompt is suppressed for `--dry-run`, `--no-save`, `--no-walk`,
recommendations.body: `RUNBOOK.md` § "Reuse-last-review prompt" ends with "The prompt is suppressed for `--dry-run`, `--no-save`, `--no-walk`, `--step N`, and non-TTY contexts (CI / pipes)", grouping non-TTY with the hard opt-outs that return no path at all. On non-TTY stdin `_prompt_reuse_saved_review()` auto-accepts an eligible fresh save and `_cmd_review_body()` prints its findings and exits 0 with no Claude call, so an operator reading this paragraph expects a fresh audit in CI and gets a reused one. It also contradicts `RUNBOOK.md` § "Reusing a saved reconcile (`--reuse`)" ("auto-decides under `--yes` / non-TTY stdin") and `docs/cli/reconcile-plan.md`'s `--reuse` row
recommendations.suggested_action: in `RUNBOOK.md` § "Reuse-last-review prompt", move non-TTY out of the suppression list and state that non-TTY stdin auto-accepts an eligible fresh save, prints its findings, and skips the per-finding walk
